doc.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 2, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Wanting a better work/life balance after years on the road
summary: Monk mentions lugging gear; Nicki says she was addicted to being busy and wants to schedule more time at home between tours.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: I’m trying to figure out how to phrase this question, I’ll use my own experience as an example. Most of the gigs I play I have to move gear.
I have a full sized digital keyboard and this and that. And that I don’t miss.
You know me too. I have to say my back’s been better.
Do you think there could be things that you will reconsider even doing when hopefully we get back to normal?
Yes I think I’ve found that I do need a better work/life balance. I wasn’t handling that well. I think every musician struggles with this. We don’t like to say no.
Yes. A gig is a gig.

A gig is a gig, we like the routine of being busy and being on the road. You know? We get addicted to it, and I was addicted to it. And I’ve found that I do need more of a work/life balance. I’m not — I’m a long way from 30, you know what I mean? And you just don’t think about things when you’re younger and now it’s like well I can use time off to do more things here at home. And so I do want to find that. I mean we don’t know what we’re going back to. And I certainly want to work on other things here, getting back to the question. Sorry I went way off the question. You know that’s the big takeaway for me is I need to be better at scheduling so that I am at home more between, especially big tours. Five, six weeks now, that sounds like a long time. And it was nothing for me you know? Go out for five or six weeks, no problem.
